texts: good. the walk, Meren Tallowhand as the walker, the station as the destination, the station's position on the Cliff Path, sundown, the year and the one-day gap to the autumn equinox are all carried. 'the late summer of Year 1' is improvised as a season symbol beside the year term, but nothing in it is lost.

good. lighting the lantern parses as a plain past event with Meren as the agent, the lantern as the thing acted on and the station as the location, and 'the station' is correctly tied back to the station of the first sentence.
good. the lantern is the agent, mire-essence the consumed object, and 'mire-essence' is unpacked to its genus 'essence'.
good. the producing event, the lantern as the agent and mist-light as what is produced all come through, with 'mist-light' unpacked to its genus 'light'.

bad: 'The mist-light' is a specific thing — the light this lantern has just made — but the parse puts the bare kind symbol mist_light in the attracting event's agent slot instead of a typed individual, so the light in this sentence is never linked to the one the previous sentence produced, and one symbol ends up in both a class position and an individual position. Introduce it as an individual in the previous sentence and refer back to it here: "The lantern produced a mist-light." followed by "The mist-light attracted nightmoths."

good. the seventeen nightmoths land as a counted group, the counting has Meren as the agent and the lantern as its location, and 'the third watch' keeps its ordinal rank. the watch time is routed through a minted watch entity rather than a plain time constant, which is an encoding wrinkle on our side and not a problem with your wording.

good. 'a handful' is recorded as a vague count on a group of nightmoths with no number invented, the gathering stays one collective event at the Middle Row, and 'that night' correctly picks up the year from the earlier sentences.

mixed: the universal over the sky-cats, the cliff-spires, the night and the past tense all come through, but 'stayed' loses its continuation — the parse says only that each sky-cat was on the cliff-spires that night, not that it was already there and remained — and the cliff-spires are filed under a bare preposition head instead of the event's location slot, so a 'where were they?' question will not find them. Make the continuation explicit with 'still', which we do have a carrier for: "All the sky-cats were still on the cliff-spires that night."
